SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 2-day history of central lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain; feels intermittently hot and sweaty.  
- Symptom history:
  • Pain location: mid-line lower abdomen.  
  • No previous similar episodes.  
  • Associated mild nausea; no vomiting.  
  • Bowel: constipation last week, currently resolved; last bowel movement 2 hrs ago, normal; no rectal bleeding.  
  • Urinary: increased frequency; single episode of pink-tinged urine; no dysuria, no flank/back pain, no malodorous urine.  
  • Temperature self-checked 1 hr ago 37 °C; no documented fever.  
  • No vaginal discharge, inter-menstrual bleeding, or post-coital bleeding.  
  • No recent travel.  

- Past medical history: Denies significant medical problems (only common colds/flu).  
- Past surgical/gynecologic history: Prior contraceptive implant removed one year ago.  
- Medications: None regular.  
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not specified).  
- Social history: Lives with parents. Non-smoker. Alcohol: ~1 beer, 4 times per week.  
- Family history: Mother—breast cancer (treated, in remission).

Objective:
- Vitals (self-reported): Temperature 37 °C; no other vitals available.  
- No physical examination performed (telehealth).  
- Investigations: None performed; no urinalysis or imaging.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain / possible urinary tract infection (UTI)
   - Assessment: Suspected uncomplicated lower UTI (cystitis).
   - Differential diagnosis: Early pyelonephritis, gynecologic pathology (e.g., early PID), gastrointestinal cause (e.g., irritable bowel, early appendicitis) — low clinical suspicion currently.
   - Investigations planned: None arranged at this encounter; consider urinalysis ± culture if symptoms persist or worsen.
   - Treatment planned: Empiric oral antibiotic course for 3 days, to be taken twice daily (drug, dose, route not documented). Safety-net provided.
   - Referrals: Face-to-face review if deteriorating, high fever, back pain, or persistent/recurrent symptoms.

Quality checks:

• Missing but clinically expected:
  – Detailed allergy reaction to amoxicillin.  
  – Full vitals (BP, HR, RR, oxygen saturation).  
  – Pregnancy status in reproductive-age female.  
  – Urinalysis and urine culture prior to antibiotics.  
  – Exact antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency.

• Internal conflicts: None noted.

• Transcript quality: Clear; minor background pauses but clinically adequate.
